## Approval

<!-- parity: /approval /allow -->

User file top-level keys:

```yaml
approvalMode: yolo             # always-ask | write | yolo | unattended
allowedTools:                  # always-allow list (exec tier still honors critical patterns per mode)
  - web_fetch
```

CLI equivalent: `/approval <mode>`, `/allow <tool>` — both persist to these
keys. Applies at next boot (the running session keeps its live mode).

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Mode

<!-- parity: /mode /code /architect /review -->

User file top-level key:

```yaml
mode: code                     # code | architect | review
```

CLI equivalent: `/mode <name>` or the `/code`, `/architect`, `/review`
shortcuts — they switch live AND persist this key.

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Prompts, TTSR & A2A

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
a2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints
  servers:
    peer:
      url: https://peer.example:8080
      token: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value]}      # env-resolved at boot — never a literal secret
fabric:                         # host discovery announcements (read-only:
  capabilities:                 # written by hosts, never user-edited)
    - name: yoclip.render
      description: Render the open project to MP4
```

`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they
configure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\${ENV}` reference
resolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an
unset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.

## Settings hub

<!-- parity: /settings -->

`/settings` is an interactive hub over the surfaces above (provider, model,
approval, cube, keys, MCP, DAP hub). It has no single config equivalent —
each arm edits the section documented for it. DAP hub settings are the one
surface NOT in config.yaml: the hub flow writes `~/.dap/config.json`
(identity keys, channels). Configure DAP through the hub flow or see
docs/dap.md; never hand-edit the DAP files while a hub client is running.

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for
the run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI's, so ssh
sessions show the model's reasoning as it happens. The default `false`
keeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic
`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits
silent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use
(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless
`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no
flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml
output:
  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

Applies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file
reads, fast boot):

```yaml
projectContext:
  maxBytes: 32768 # merged budget; 0 = section off, no file reads
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for
product/store links — the App Store banner in the web/macOS apps, the
CLI, and the fa1.dev site generator all resolve the same values, so a
link changes in ONE place. Defaults are baked in; only overrides are
written. Strict parse: a non-map section, a non-URL value, or a
non-boolean banner is a `ConfigException`; unknown keys become notes,
never failures:

```yaml
links:
  appstore: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163
  testflight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK
  site: https://fa1.dev
  banner: true # false = no in-app App Store banner anywhere
```

`play:` (the Google Play release) stays ABSENT until the Android release
is live — every surface renders the Android slot as "coming soon" while
it is unset.

`banner: false` is the regression switch: the Get surface stays
byte-identical to the legacy UI. The section is user-file only (like
`tui:`/`fabric:`) and applies at next boot for the in-app banner; the
site renders the committed defaults (regen:
`dart run scripts/regen_site_store_block.dart`).

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

# [GOAL] fix(codemie): legacy /code-assistant-api/ entries without authMethod should auto-run SSO — draft for issue [#2424](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/2424)

## Goal — a legacy CodeMie entry behaves exactly like a freshly created SSO entry (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **a saved custom-provider entry pointing at a `/code-assistant-api/` endpoint that predates the `authMethod` field becomes, at read time, indistinguishable from an entry freshly created by the SSO flow — every classification site routes it to SSO, and selecting it opens browser login when the cookie is missing or expired.**

Today `authMethod` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart:46-59`: `apiKey | sso | jwt`, defaulting to `apiKey` at `:72`; parse at `:151-161` — absent, non-string, or unknown values all fold to `apiKey`) was introduced after CodeMie SSO shipped. Entries saved before it carry no `authMethod:` key and parse as `apiKey`. The SSO matcher `_findCodeMieSsoEntry` (`lib/src/cli/codemie_provider_commands.dart:48-498`) requires `authMethod == sso` with NO URL-marker fallback, so boot restore (`_restoreCodeMieCookieAuthIfNeeded`, `:465-486`, called from `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:1134`) never wires cookie auth for legacy entries — the stored cookie goes out as `Authorization: Bearer`, which CodeMie rejects with a 302 redirect to the SSO portal (the doc comment at `:455-460` names exactly this failure). The user only recovers after a failed request: interactive runs self-heal via `_maybeHandleCodeMieError` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart:247-254` → `_handleCodeMieAuthExpired` `:312-323`, browser relaunch), headless runs surface the error and exit non-zero. Selecting a model on the legacy entry therefore does not open browser login up front — the failure happens on the wire first. Other `authMethod` consumers with the same hole: export key-kind classification (`_transferKeyKind`, `lib/src/cli/provider_export_command.dart:152-162` — a legacy entry exports as plain `apiKey` kind). The fix per issue [#2424](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/2424): match by the URL marker in `codemie_provider_commands.dart`.

## Why this framing

  - The framing is read-time equivalence, not migration: legacy entries must never need a one-time conversion to behave correctly. A "repair the file first" framing would leave every not-yet-repaired machine broken and would rewrite user config on load (rejected — see Non-goals).
  - The framing is classification-site-wide, not just boot restore: `_findCodeMieSsoEntry` is the only `authMethod`-gated SSO match in `codemie_provider_commands.dart`, but the same legacy-blindness pattern exists in export (`_transferKeyKind`); fixing one site while the export classifies the same entry as a plain key would produce divergent behavior per surface — the whole class of mistake gets fixed (hard rule: a correction is never a one-line fix).
  - No earlier framing exists to retract; this is the initial draft.

## Architecture

**Named rule — the marker-match classification.** One predicate decides CodeMie-ness of a saved entry:

> **RULE-M:** an entry is CodeMie iff `isCodeMieBaseUrl(entry.baseUrl)` — the case-insensitive `/code-assistant-api(/|$)` regex at `lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:50-52`.

RULE-M replaces the scattered spellings for SSO classification. Today the tree uses `.contains('/code-assistant-api/')` in ~10 sites (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:143, 249, 351, 495`; `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart:231, 297`; `lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart:542`; `lib/src/providers/models_for_endpoint.dart:313`; `lib/src/cli/provider_export_command.dart:159`). The two predicates DISAGREE on two input classes (pinned facts, each needs a positive + negative test):

  - `…/code-assistant-api` **without** `/v1` (which `codeMieApiBase` normalization produces, `codemie_sso.dart:33-40`, and which the SSO flow's own fixture uses — `test/integration/codemie_sso_integration_test.dart:93`): the regex matches, `contains` does not.
  - a `-proxy` twin (`…/code-assistant-api-proxy/…`, someone's own service on a marker-shaped path): `contains` matches, the regex (`(/|$)` boundary) does not — the regex is the false-positive-safe choice.

**Named precedence — explicit authMethod always wins (RULE-P):**

 <markdown-accessiblity-table>

|  Stored `authMethod` |  Marker (RULE-M) |  Resolved auth path |
| --- | --- | --- |

|  `sso` |  any |  SSO — never overridden |

|  `jwt` |  any |  JWT Bearer — never overridden |

|  **absent** (legacy) |  yes |  **SSO — the fix** |

|  absent |  no |  plain entry — unchanged behavior |

|  `apiKey` (explicit) |  yes |  legacy-SSO candidate, token-shape-guarded (see E3/OQ2) |

</markdown-accessiblity-table>

RULE-P is absolute: the marker NEVER overrides an explicit `sso`/`jwt` value. A user who deliberately re-authenticated an entry as JWT keeps JWT after this card.

**Classification sites the rule applies to (core):**

  1. `_findCodeMieSsoEntry` (`codemie_provider_commands.dart:48-498`) — boot restore and live re-apply (`_restoreCodeMieCookieAuthIfNeeded` `:465-486`, `_applyCodeMieCookieAuth` `:517-541`). With RULE-M+RULE-P: match by marker, explicit `jwt`/`apiKey`-with-JWT-shaped-token excluded.
  2. `_switchToSavedCodeMieProvider` (`:402-431`) — the saved-entry switch dispatch. Already marker-routed by its caller (`_switchToSavedProvider`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:493-498`); its JWT leg (`:407`: `authMethod == jwt || isCodeMieJwtToken(token)`) keeps the token-shape guard for the ambiguous legacy case; its SSO leg restarts the browser flow on missing/expired cookie (`:414-421`) — this is the "selecting the model opens browser login" path: `/model` cross-provider picks land here via `_maybeSwitchToSavedEntry` (`lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart:397-404`) and picker picks via `_tuiPickSavedProvider` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:143-145`).
  3. `_transferKeyKind` (`lib/src/cli/provider_export_command.dart:152-162`) — export/export-import fidelity: marker + absent → `ProviderTransferKeyKind.sso`, so a legacy entry's credential round-trips as the SSO kind it actually is.
  4. Edit-wizard re-auth offer (`_editReauthOption`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:139-145`) — already marker-based; pinned as the reference shape, not changed.

**Migration policy (pinned): read-time matching only.** No load-time rewrite of config.yaml. Repair-on-write already happens naturally: every SSO save/re-login stamps `authMethod: sso` (`lib/src/cli/provider_codemie_sso.dart:113`), every JWT connect stamps `jwt` (`codemie_provider_commands.dart:312`), and `toYaml` always writes the field (`custom_providers.dart:218`) — so a legacy entry becomes a modern one the first time its user re-authenticates, with zero migration code.

**Invariants:**

  - **INV-1** — "explicit wins": no classification site may resolve an entry with explicit `authMethod: sso|jwt` to anything else. Asserted by UT.
  - **INV-2** — "no writes at read": config load, boot restore, model-select, and export never mutate config.yaml. Asserted by an IT that byte-compares the config file before/after the flows.
  - **INV-3** — "no new false positives": a non-CodeMie entry (no marker) classifies exactly as today. Asserted by UT truth table.
  - **INV-4** — "browser login is interactive-only": headless runs never attempt the browser; they surface the auth error with non-zero exit (existing `_headlessMode` gate, `agent_cli_run.dart:249-250`). The fix changes WHO gets proactively routed, never WHETHER headless opens a browser.

**Fallback path:** for an ambiguous legacy entry (absent authMethod) whose stored token is JWT-shaped, `isCodeMieJwtToken` (`codemie_sso.dart`) still routes the switch to the JWT leg — the shape guard stays as the tie-breaker under the marker (E3).

**Core (this card):** RULE-M + RULE-P applied at sites 1-3; the marker rule pinned as the regex predicate at those sites; tests.

**Second tier (opt-in, follow-up friendly):** consolidating every `.contains('/code-assistant-api/')` spelling onto `isCodeMieBaseUrl` tree-wide (one grep-audited predicate); the `-proxy` negative test rides it.

**Excluded (with rationale):**

  - *Bulk config rewrite on load* — INV-2; the issue is read-time by construction, and write-on-load would surprise every tool that diffs config.yaml.
  - *A migration CLI verb* — unnecessary once read-time matching lands (re-auth self-heals the stored shape); revisit only if OQ1 lands as repair-on-load.
  - *Distinguishing absent vs explicit `apiKey` in the parsed entry object* — a schema-adjacent change (`_parseAuthMethod` folds both to one value, `custom_providers.dart:151-161`); only needed if the owner resolves OQ2 with strict honoring, so it is optioned there, not built here.
  - *App-side changes* — the app never reads `authMethod`; its marker routing already treats legacy entries as CodeMie.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

  - **AC1** — a legacy entry (marker URL, no `authMethod` key on disk) resolves to the SSO path at every core classification site: boot restore wires cookie auth; a missing/expired cookie launches the SSO flow (browser login opens) instead of sending the cookie as Bearer. Hook: line-mode IT with `codeMieSsoAuthenticateFn` seam + config-file fixture lacking `authMethod` (the `test/cli/codemie_setup_test.dart` harness).
  - **AC2** — boot on a legacy entry with a VALID stored cookie: chat requests go out as `Cookie:`-header auth (no `Authorization: Bearer`), identical to a freshly created SSO entry's first request. Hook: IT capturing the outgoing headers through the fake stream function.
  - **AC3** — RULE-P holds: entries with explicit `authMethod: sso` and `authMethod: jwt` classify exactly as today under the new matcher (positive + negative tests both directions; `jwt` never hijacked to SSO, `sso` never demoted). Hook: UT on the classification function + IT on the switch dispatch.
  - **AC4** — export fidelity: a legacy entry exports with the SSO transfer-key kind; its re-import behaves as SSO. Hook: UT on `_transferKeyKind` with a legacy-shaped entry.
  - **AC5** — a non-CodeMie entry (no marker; including a `-proxy` marker-shaped twin) is never routed to SSO, with or without `authMethod`. Hook: UT truth table (RULE-M positives/negatives).
  - **AC6** — read-only guarantee: boot, model-select, and export over a legacy entry leave config.yaml byte-identical. Hook: IT byte-compare (INV-2).
  - **AC7** — surface parity REG: CLI (boot restore + switch + model-select) and the app's marker-based routing agree on legacy entries — selecting the model opens SSO on both. Hook: REG guards below.

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

  - **UT-1** (→ AC1/AC3, RULE-M×RULE-P truth table) — pure classification: `{absent, apiKey, sso, jwt, 'bogus'→apiKey}` × `{marker, non-marker, /v1-less marker, -proxy twin}` → resolved path. This is the one table every site must satisfy.
  - **UT-2** (→ AC5) — pure: `isCodeMieBaseUrl` vs `.contains` divergence cases pinned (the `/v1`-less positive and the `-proxy` negative).
  - **UT-3** (→ AC4) — pure: `_transferKeyKind` with legacy entry → SSO kind; explicit `jwt` entry → apiKey kind (existing mapping preserved).
  - **UT-4** (→ AC3) — pure: `_parseAuthMethod` folds unknown/absent to `apiKey` (documented input to the truth table).
  - **IT-1** (→ AC1) — line-mode boot with a legacy fixture entry and an EXPIRED cookie: browser SSO restart fires at boot (before any request), mirroring `_restoreCodeMieCookieAuthIfNeeded`'s expired branch; with `codeMieSsoAuthenticateFn` faked.
  - **IT-2** (→ AC2) — line-mode boot, legacy entry, valid cookie: outgoing chat headers carry `cookie:` and no Bearer; byte-equal to the fresh-SSO-entry control run in the same test (semantic-drift property: legacy vs modern differ only in the on-disk yaml, never in behavior).
  - **IT-3** (→ AC1, the headline) — `/model` select onto a legacy CodeMie entry with missing/expired credential: the SSO flow opens (browser launch faked), the guided project→model flow runs, the entry re-saves stamped `authMethod: sso` (repair-on-write observed, not forced).
  - **IT-4** (→ AC3) — switch dispatch: legacy entry with a JWT-shaped token → JWT leg (no browser); explicit `jwt` entry → JWT leg; explicit `sso` entry with expired cookie → browser. All through `_switchToSavedCodeMieProvider` seams.
  - **IT-5** (→ AC6) — byte-compare config.yaml across boot + model-select + export over a legacy entry (INV-2).
  - **IT-6** (→ AC4) — export/import round-trip of a legacy entry: kind preserved, re-import runs SSO on the importing machine.
  - **E2E-1** (→ AC1/AC7) — real `fa` boot against a recorded fake CodeMie endpoint: legacy fixture, first turn succeeds via cookie auth (no 302 episode in the log).
  - **REG-1** (→ AC7, CLI) — regression guard: legacy entries classify as SSO at boot restore, switch, model-select, and export — the four sites pinned in ONE test file so a new classification site that forgets RULE-M turns red. **A red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
  - **REG-2** (→ AC7, app) — Flutter-app guard: the app's marker routing (`isCodeMieProvider`) accepts the `/v1`-less marker spelling (the RULE-M regex), so CLI and app never disagree on a legacy entry's CodeMie-ness.
  - **REG-3** (→ AC3) — sibling-provider guard: an OpenRouter/AIIN entry (no marker) is byte-unchanged in classification after the card — no marker bleed into other providers' routing.

**CI wiring:** UT/IT in the per-PR gate; REG-1/REG-3 in the CLI shard; REG-2 in the app workflow. Merge rule: **REG red = merge blocked**, independent of IT/E2E.

### Edge / border cases

  - **E1** — legacy entry with NO stored credential (keyless / cleared secure-store slot): resolves SSO → cookie missing → browser login opens at boot/select (not a silent Bearer of an empty key). Pinned by IT-1 variant.
  - **E2** — URL spelling variance: `…/code-assistant-api` (no `/v1`), `…/code-assistant-api/`, `…/code-assistant-api/v1`, mixed-case host/path — all RULE-M positives; the SSO org-URL derivation (`codeMieOrgUrl`, `codemie_sso.dart:57-59`) must handle each when relaunching login. Pinned in UT-2 + IT-3 variant.
  - **E3** — ambiguous token on a legacy entry: JWT-shaped stored value → JWT leg (shape guard wins inside the marker branch); cookie-shaped (`k=v;…`) or missing → SSO leg. The `_resolveCodeMieCookie` fallback (`codemie_provider_commands.dart:501-515`) accepts only cookie-shaped legacy `apiKey` values — a raw API key on a legacy entry is NOT valid cookie auth and must not be sent as one. Pinned in IT-4.
  - **E4** — explicit `authMethod: apiKey` on a marker URL (a user who wants Bearer auth against CodeMie, e.g. `CODEMIE_API_KEY`-style): with today's parse this is indistinguishable from absent (OQ2). Pinned interim behavior: marker + `apiKey` + cookie-shaped/JWT-shaped token resolves per E3; a raw non-cookie, non-JWT token surfaces the SSO/login path rather than a silent mis-shaped Bearer. Final behavior is OQ2.
  - **E5** — `authMethod: 'none'` or any unknown string: parses to `apiKey` (`custom_providers.dart:151-161`) → treated as legacy under the marker (E4 rule). There is no `none` intent value in the schema; if a user wrote one, it was never a distinct signal. Pinned in UT-4.
  - **E6** — false positive: a NON-CodeMie provider deliberately saved under a marker-shaped URL (self-hosted service behind `…/code-assistant-api-proxy/`): RULE-M's regex rejects the `-proxy` twin (negative test); a TRUE marker URL on a non-CodeMie service is not diagnosable client-side — the legacy-absent case would route it SSO, and the documented escape hatch is setting `authMethod: jwt`/`apiKey` explicitly (RULE-P honored). Pinned in UT-2/UT-1.
  - **E7** — duplicated entries on the same endpoint (e.g. `codemie` and `codemie:2` names, same baseUrl, one legacy one modern): classification is per-entry (RULE-M × RULE-P evaluated on each); matches resolve in registry order with `firstOrNull` semantics preserved (`_findCodeMieSsoEntry` today). No cross-entry inference — a modern sibling never rewrites a legacy twin's classification. Pinned in UT-1 variant + IT-2.
  - **E8** — headless/`--no-browser` on a legacy entry with expired cookie: no browser attempt; the auth-expired error surfaces and the run exits non-zero (INV-4). Pinned in IT-1 headless variant.
  - **E9** — kill/resume: a session restored mid-SSO-restart resumes with the entry still legacy; the next boot re-classifies identically (classification is a pure function of the entry — no hidden state). Pinned by IT-2's determinism (same fixture → same classification on every run).

## Non-goals

  - **No bulk config rewrite on load** — read-time matching only (INV-2, AC6); the stored yaml gains `authMethod` only through the user's own next save/re-login (repair-on-write as it exists today).
  - No migration CLI verb and no one-shot converter in this card (see Excluded; revisit only via OQ1).
  - No changes to explicit-`authMethod` behavior (RULE-P — a deliberate `jwt` or `sso` entry is untouched).
  - No app-side changes — the Flutter app has no `authMethod` surface and already routes by marker.
  - No new authMethod values, no schema changes to `CustomProviderEntry` (OQ2's sentinel is optioned, not built).
  - No changes to the reactive mid-stream recovery (`_maybeHandleCodeMieError`) — it stays as the belt under the now-proactive routing.

## Open questions (owner decisions)

  - **OQ1 — repair-on-read vs repair-on-write.** The card pins read-time matching with natural repair-on-write (re-login stamps `authMethod: sso`). Alternative: a load-time normalization that stamps `authMethod: sso` onto marker entries missing the field (makes the file self-describing, enables strict OQ2 honoring, but writes config on boot — contradicts INV-2 and would need a "changed on boot" notice). Options: (a) keep read-time only [recommended]; (b) normalize-on-load with a boot note; (c) normalize-on-load silent. Owner call.
  - **OQ2 — explicit `authMethod: apiKey` on a marker URL.** Today's parser cannot distinguish "explicitly apiKey" from "field absent" (both fold to `apiKey`, `custom_providers.dart:151-161`). Options: (a) fold both into legacy-SSO under the marker [this card's pinned interim behavior — matches the issue's population, risks hijacking a deliberate apiKey-on-CodeMie setup]; (b) add a parse-level explicitness sentinel so only ABSENT gets marker routing and explicit `apiKey` is honored verbatim [strictest reading of RULE-P; needs the schema-adjacent change excluded above]; (c) keep the token-shape heuristic as the only tie-breaker and document `jwt` as the escape hatch. Owner call — (b) is the semantically clean end state if any user is known to run key-based auth against a CodeMie endpoint.
  - **OQ3 — export scope.** Should `_transferKeyKind`'s legacy→SSO reclassification (AC4) ship in this card or in a follow-up export-fidelity card? Shipping here keeps classification single-sourced; deferring keeps this card strictly inside `codemie_provider_commands.dart` as the issue scopes it. Owner call.

# gh-2424 plan — legacy `/code-assistant-api/` entries without authMethod auto-run SSO

Ticket: entries saved before `authMethod` existed parse as the `apiKey`
default and were never treated as SSO — selecting the model did not open
browser login. Fix per the issue card: match by the URL marker
(RULE-M) with explicit-authMethod-wins precedence (RULE-P), read-time
only (no config writes).

## Tasks

### T1 — failing classification tests (boot restore + select dispatch) [RED]
- what: add `group('legacy CodeMie entries classify as SSO (gh-2424)')` in
  `test/cli/codemie_setup_test.dart` driving the two CLI-observable
  classification surfaces: (a) boot restore (`_restoreCodeMieCookieAuthIfNeeded`
  via AgentCli construction — legacy + valid cookie wires `cookie:` headers;
  `/v1`-less marker URL wires too; `-proxy` twin does NOT; explicit `jwt`
  never wires; entry stays unmutated = read-time guarantee), (b) select
  dispatch (`/provider <name>` — legacy + raw non-cookie non-JWT token
  restarts SSO instead of sending it mis-shaped; legacy + JWT-shaped token
  takes the JWT leg, no browser).
- verify: `dart test test/cli/codemie_setup_test.dart` — new tests FAIL
  (boot wiring absent, raw key mis-sent as cookie), existing 23 stay green.

### T2 — `_findCodeMieSsoEntry` matches by the URL marker (RULE-M×RULE-P) [GREEN]
- what: in `lib/src/cli/codemie_provider_commands.dart` rewrite the matcher:
  require `isCodeMieBaseUrl(e.baseUrl)` (the `/code-assistant-api(/|$)`
  regex — accepts the `/v1`-less spelling, rejects `-proxy` twins), admit
  `authMethod != jwt` (so + legacy apiKey default), exclude entries whose
  resolved credential is JWT-shaped (JWT rides Bearer, never a Cookie
  header). Add the cookie-shape helper and the E4 guard in
  `_restoreCodeMieCookieAuthIfNeeded`: a legacy (non-explicit-so) entry
  whose resolved credential is neither cookie-shaped nor JWT-shaped goes to
  the SO restart branch instead of being applied as a cookie.
- verify: T1 boot-restore tests go green; full codemie_setup_test.dart green.

### T3 — select dispatch + SO leg shape guard [GREEN]
- what: in `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart` `_switchToSavedProvider`
  route via `isCodeMieBaseUrl(entry.baseUrl)` instead of
  `.contains('/code-assistant-api/')`; in `_switchToSavedCodeMieProvider`
  (codemie_provider_commands.dart) extend the SO-leg restart condition with
  the E4 raw-token guard for non-explicit-so entries.
- verify: T1 select-dispatch tests go green; existing legacy `/v1` select
  test (expired cookie → re-run SSO) stays green.

### T4 — failing export-kind test + `_transferKeyKind` fix [RED→GREEN]
- what: in `test/cli/provider_transfer_test.dart` add: legacy CodeMie entry
  exports with `ProviderTransferKeyKind.sso` (round-trip prompt shows
  `(sso)`); explicit `jwt` entry still exports `api-key` (no-regression).
  Then in `lib/src/cli/provider_export_command.dart` `_transferKeyKind`:
  marker via `isCodeMieBaseUrl`, `jwt → apiKey` kind, `so`/legacy → `sso` kind.
- verify: both new tests green; existing transfer tests green.

### T5 — full gate run
- what: `dart analyze` clean on touched files + full `dart test test/cli` +
  broader suite for regressions; format.
- verify: analyze clean; no failing tests; commit series on `ai/gh-2424`.

## Decisions
- Read-time classification only (INV-2): no load-time rewrite of
  config.yaml; repair-on-write stays the natural re-auth stamp.
- Explicit `authMethod: sso|jwt` always wins (RULE-P); the marker only
  upgrades the legacy `apiKey` default. Token-shape is the tie-breaker for
  ambiguous legacy values (JWT-shaped → JWT leg; cookie-shaped → SSO leg;
  raw non-cookie non-JWT → SSO login path rather than a mis-shaped send —
  the card's E3/E4 pinned interim).
- Boot restore with a MISSING cookie stays silent (same as fresh `sso`
  entries today): legacy must behave exactly like a fresh entry, and
  boot-time browser popups for keyless entries stay out of scope; the
  select path and reactive recovery cover that case.
- Export kind: only the legacy class changes (`apiKey` → `sso` kind);
  explicit `jwt`/`sso` mappings preserved (UT-3).
- App-side (`isCodeMieProvider` in flutter_app) untouched — the card
  excludes app changes; `/v1`-less predicate consolidation tree-wide is the
  card's opt-in second tier, deferred.
- Second-tier `.contains` → `isCodeMieBaseUrl` consolidation at unrelated
  sites (quota, models fetch, setup wizard) deferred: opt-in follow-up,
  not core.

## Open questions
- OQ2 (explicit apiKey on a marker URL) — unresolved owner call; pinned
  interim = fold into legacy-SSO under the marker with the token-shape
  tie-breaker (matches the issue population; escape hatch: set
  `authMethod: jwt` explicitly).
- OQ3 (export scope) — resolved to ship in this card (AC4 keeps
  classification single-sourced); the card allows either.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

Hmm — actually in Dart, `dart test` with tag configs: tags are only EXCLUDED when configured with `skip` or via CLI `--exclude-tags`. The comments say "excluded from the default pre-commit gate" for io; the gate presumably passes explicit exclude flags. What does the pre-commit hook run? `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` — for lib/bin/test paths: "+tests" — let me check what test command the gate uses, and run THAT (grader parity: the gate is the project's canonical verifier).

# gh-2424 — legacy `/code-assistant-api/` entries without `authMethod` auto-run SSO ### What changed Legacy CodeMie entries (saved before `authMethod` existed — they parse as the `apiKey` default) now classify as SSO cookie auth at every read-time classification site, matched by the `/code-assistant-api(/|$)` URL marker (`isCodeMieBaseUrl`) instead of the missing field. Boot restore wires cookie auth for them exactly like a fresh `sso` entry, and selecting the model on a missing/expired cookie opens the SSO browser login instead of failing on the wire with a 302. ### Key decisions - RULE-M × RULE-P: the marker decides CodeMie-ness; an explicit `authMethod: sso|jwt` always wins; a JWT-shaped stored token is the tie-breaker (rides Bearer, never a Cookie header). - Read-time classification only — config.yaml is never rewritten on load; re-auth naturally repairs the entry (repair-on-write as before). - Shape guard (card E3/E4): a legacy entry whose stored value is neither cookie-shaped nor JWT-shaped goes to the SSO login path instead of being sent as a mis-shaped credential; explicit `sso` entries keep today's verbatim behavior. - `_switchToSavedProvider` and `_transferKeyKind` (export) upgraded from `.contains('/code-assistant-api/')` to the pinned regex — the `/v1`-less spelling now routes correctly; a legacy entry exports as the `sso` transfer-key kind (explicit `jwt` keeps `api-key`). - Tree-wide `.contains` consolidation and the Flutter-app predicate are the card's opt-in second tier — deliberately deferred. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/codemie_setup_test.dart test/cli/provider_transfer_test.dart ``` All 8 new tests in `legacy CodeMie entries classify as SSO (gh-2424)` + 2 export-kind tests; 72 total in the two files, green.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD SEL["/provider · /model pick"] --> DISP{_switchToSavedProvider:
isCodeMieBaseUrl?} DISP -->|yes| CM[_switchToSavedCodeMieProvider] DISP -->|no| GEN[regular switch] CM -->|authMethod jwt · JWT-shaped token| JWT[JWT Bearer leg] CM -->|so · legacy · cookie-shaped/missing/expired| SSO[SSO leg → browser login] BOOT["boot restore"] --> M{_findCodeMieSsoEntry:
marker + RULE-P} M -->|match| COOKIE[wire cookie headers · expired → SSO] M -->|no match| PLAIN[unchanged] EXP["/provider export"] --> TK{_transferKeyKind} TK -->|marker + so/legacy| SSO_KIND[sso kind] TK -->|marker + jwt| KEY[api-key kind] ```
